where: Section 1, after the definition of Sᵢⱼ
problem: The sentence repeats itself: 'The array S is the scattering matrix; some syllabi call it the scattering matrix.' A student stops and wonders whether two different names are meant.
fix: Keep one naming sentence, e.g. 'The array S is the scattering matrix; some syllabi call it the S-matrix.'

problem: Read literally, 'the phase of every S-parameter touching that port changes by e^{−jβl}' gives the wrong answer for the diagonal term Sᵢᵢ, which touches the same port at both ends and so picks up e^{−j2βl}. Only the off-diagonal terms touching the port once get a single factor.
fix: Say: 'moving port i outward by l multiplies Sᵢⱼ by e^{−jβl} for each end of the parameter that sits at port i; so Sᵢⱼ (i≠j) gains e^{−jβl} and Sᵢᵢ gains e^{−j2βl}.'

problem: The 'Meaning' column describes return loss as 'Power reflected back at the input' and insertion loss as 'Power lost in forward transmission'. Both are dB ratios, not powers; a student may think RL is the reflected power in watts.
fix: Return loss: 'dB ratio of incident to reflected power at the input; larger RL means a smaller reflection.' Insertion loss: 'dB ratio of incident to transmitted power; larger IL means more loss.'
